what_its_for: This eye drop medicine is used to treat certain types of glaucoma (a condition where pressure inside your eye is too high) and a condition called accommodative esotropia (a type of crossed eyes in children caused by a focusing problem). It works by helping fluid drain out of the eye to lower eye pressure, and by helping your eyes focus better.
how_to_take: Wash your hands well before using. Tilt your head back and gently pull your lower eyelid down to form a small pocket. Hold the dropper above your eye and squeeze the prescribed number of drops into the pocket. Close your eye gently and press your finger against the inner corner of your eye (near your nose) for 1 to 2 minutes — this helps keep the medicine in your eye and reduces side effects. Do not let the dropper tip touch your eye, fingers, or any other surface. Replace the cap tightly after each use. If you wear contact lenses, remove them before using the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in.
dosing: Your doctor will tell you exactly how many drops to use and how often. Most patients use 1 drop in the affected eye(s) once or twice a day, or sometimes every other day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions since the dose is adjusted based on your condition. Do not use more drops or use them more often than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use the drops as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not use a double dose to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store the unmixed powder in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C). Once the solution is mixed and ready to use, it can be kept in the refrigerator for up to 6 months, or at room temperature (below 77°F / 25°C) for up to 1 month. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze the solution. Throw away any unused solution after the expiration date or as directed by your pharmacist.
what_to_avoid: Avoid touching the dropper tip to any surface to prevent contamination. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery right after using these drops, as they may cause blurry vision or difficulty seeing in dim light — especially when you first start using them. Avoid exposure to certain pesticides and insecticides (such as those used in gardening or farming) while using this medicine, as they work in a similar way and can cause serious side effects when combined. Tell all of your doctors, including surgeons and anesthesiologists, that you are using this medicine before any procedure or surgery, especially if you need general anesthesia.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: sudden severe eye pain, unusual vision changes, very slow or irregular heartbeat, muscle weakness, excessive sweating or drooling, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach cramps, difficulty breathing, dizziness, fainting, or unusual tiredness. Also contact your doctor if your eye becomes red, swollen, or irritated, or if your symptoms get worse instead of better. Seek emergency help immediately if you accidentally swallow any of the eye drops.
when_it_works: You may notice some improvement in your eye pressure or eye alignment within a few days to a couple of weeks of starting treatment. However, it may take several weeks to see the full benefit, especially for crossed eyes in children. Keep using the drops as prescribed even if you feel well, since glaucoma often has no noticeable symptoms.
special_populations: Children: This medicine is sometimes used for children with crossed eyes caused by a focusing problem. Children may be more sensitive to side effects. Parents should watch closely for any signs of unusual symptoms. Older adults: Older patients may be at greater risk for certain side effects and should be monitored closely by their doctor. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as the safety of this medicine in these situations has not been fully established. People with certain health conditions: Tell your doctor if you have a history of detached retina, asthma, slow heart rate, low blood pressure, stomach problems, Parkinson's disease, or epilepsy, as this medicine may not be appropriate for you.
